answer.rationale: Immediate competitive pricing pressure on SMB base requires direct response to prevent acute churn. memory_73 confirms promotional pricing drives acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMB segments. A standard experiment (not broad rollout) on promotional pricing allows rapid defense of at-risk cohorts while preserving ability to test complementary retention tactics (activation_messaging, simplified_onboarding) in parallel. However, promotional pricing carries downstream risk: it may train customers to expect discounts, erode brand positioning, and create dependency on price rather than value. This is flagged but justified by acute competitive threat and prior positive data. Alternative tactics (onboarding simplification, activation messaging) have weaker direct connection to price-sensitivity churn and would take longer to impact retention. Referral incentives work in established customers, not acquisition-stage SMBs under price pressure. Enterprise sales assist is mismatched to SMB emergency. The promotional pricing response is constrained to standard_experiment scope to maintain optionality and monitor for value erosion before broader rollout.
